subject: geography
title: Transport and Deposition
welcome_lead: Rivers don't just erode — they also carry and drop material. Learn the four ways rivers transport sediment and where it ends up.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography adventure on river transport (traction, suspension) and deposition.
final_note: Great work! You can now explain how rivers move and deposit material.

concepts.def: How rivers move eroded material downstream.
Large rocks rolling along the riverbed.
Small stones bouncing along the bed.
Fine particles carried within the water.
Dissolved minerals carried in the water.
When the river drops material it cannot carry.

walkthroughs.body_html:
• Traction: rolling big rocks.
  • Saltation: bouncing pebbles.
  • Suspension: fine silt floating.
  • Solution: dissolved minerals.
When a river loses energy — like during low flow or near the mouth — it can't carry its load. The heaviest material is dropped first.
Deposition creates floodplains, levees and deltas. Rich farmland often forms along these areas!
